purpose: Replace mistaken dolphin identity with existing gray shark; rebuild original mouth anatomy.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw Image 1, the exact original SLEVEJM2 009 sprite, as one polished cartoon SHARK sprite. Image 1 controls pose, mouth shape, facing, visible anatomy, framing and water occlusion. Images 2 and 3 are CHARACTER DESIGN AND DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not pose. Match the established shark: neutral medium gray skin, pale ivory jaw and underside, gill slits, bold black outlines, smooth restrained cel shading, heavy sly brows and razor-sharp triangular teeth. This is the sneaky shark character, never a friendly dolphin; no dolphin beak or rounded dolphin teeth. Pose: Upright right-facing shark, head slightly tipped downward and largely showing gray back/flank. A small upper-head eye looks right from under a sly heavy brow. Beneath it is an open toothy mouth; its lower jaw projects right, arching down at the far tip. Do not turn that mouth into one huge eye or join the upper and lower jaws into a dolphin beak. Near pectoral fin hangs low at left; a small farther fin can be seen at lower-right. Pale belly is a narrow right-hand strip. Preserve the mouth/jaw angle and source waterline. Preserve the source silhouette and relative positions while replacing pixel steps with smooth ink. Only the character parts above water are drawn, with a thin cyan-and-white ripple at original cutoff. Do not complete submerged body, tail or legs. One character only. All contours inside canvas with clear transparent padding on every edge. Actual transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, scene, cast shadow, glow, text or collage.
